messages:
kai: Spike update: I prototyped a 'rolling-window checksum' loader that avoids heavy sidecar indexes for public streams but keeps warmup predictable. Posting the short design and tradeoffs for feedback.
alyssa: Nice name. Explain the window idea briefly.
kai: Window idea: break each shard into fixed-size windows (eg 64KB) with a tiny per-window fingerprint and a rolling-window aggregate stored in a compact header. Loader can stream-read headers cheaply, build a prioritized window manifest, and prefetch windows in priority order. Full sig verification happens async per-window.
ram: How different from stripe/delta overlays? This sounds more lightweight but potentially more windows to manage.
kai: Right 97 many small units but cheaper metadata. We treat windows as cacheable units with independent upload_hint and verify_state. Windows let us do fine-grained hotpatches by publishing a delta map that lists changed window ranges only.
marie: Integrity model? If we map a window before full verify, how do we ensure safety for regulated workloads?
ishaan: Two-mode verify: quick_fingerprint (64-bit) allowed for mapping + progressive_full_verify off-path; strict_full_verify blocks mapping until SHA256/signature completes. Default progressive for hosted/dedicated; strict enabled by policy for Private customers.
alyssa: Memory/backpressure concerns: tiny windows could flood the slab with many pending verifications.
kai: We use a window_token_pool bounded by volatile_memory_budget and max_pending_windows. Prefetch fetches only while tokens available. Also LRU on verify queue: when verify backlog grows, prefetch demotes to header-first mode.
ram: How do we avoid mixing old/new content during hotpatches?
kai: Each published manifest has an epoch token and a compact change-set map. Loader pins the epoch on open. If it observes a new epoch mid-prefetch it aborts outstanding window fetches tied to the old epoch and restarts prefetch against pinned epoch. We keep the previous epoch cached for quick rollback if overlay verification fails.
marie: What about mmap vs staged GPU upload? Windows owned by quantized layers prefer mmap+direct dma; fused-kernel windows want eager pinned upload. Windows have metadata.upload_hint = mmap|pin|staged. Loader honors hints when budget allows, else stages to pinned pool.
ishaan: Also propose a short adaptive heuristic: small windows (<16KB) prefer mmap; medium windows prefer staged; large windows prefer pin if frequent access observed.
alyssa: Operational metrics?
kai: Add window_fetch_latency, window_verify_failures, prefetch_demotions, epoch_switch_aborts, window_evictions, verify_queue_depth. Wire alerts for verify_failures > X/min and prefetch_demotions spiking.
ram: API ergonomics: ModelLoader.open(manifest_ref) -> ModelView. ModelView.snapshot_epoch() -> epoch token. ModelView.read_windows(range, policy) and lower-level WindowStream for zero-copy slices and pin_to_gpu.
marie: Testing: generate synthetic streams with base manifest + small delta maps. Inject random window corruption at 1/1000 and assert progressive detection and rollback behavior under both progressive and strict modes.
ishaan: Perf: rolling headers add one extra HTTP range read for the header per shard but massively reduces tail latency because we avoid index fetches. Need microbench to measure header+manifest assembly overhead vs index-first.
ai: rollout plan: canary on dedicated pool + internal apps for 1 week, monitor window_verify_failures and epoch_switch_aborts, then beta for opt-in public streams. Private defaults to strict.
loadbot: CI job queued: rolling-window-loader/proto (8 tests).
kai: Action items: kai push PoC branch by Tue; ishaan run verifier microbench by Thu; alyssa author E2E tests for progressive vs strict by Mon; ram wire metrics + dashboards; marie draft rollback runbook and customer migration notes.
alyssa: Thanks 97 this feels like a low-friction middle ground between full indexes and manifestless streaming.
marie: :thumbsup:
